function: Two-stage deep-unrolled network (coarse estimation net plus fine correction net) estimates the FDD downlink massive MIMO channel, exploiting intra- and inter-frame angular sparsity (pp. 3-7)
system: FDD downlink massive MIMO, one BS with M=128 antennas and one UE with N=2 antennas, no RIS, 3GPP SCM urban micro; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 8)
method: Deep unrolling of block-sparse l2,1 iterations into 8 coarse and 16 fine layers with trainable weights and thresholds; supervised layer-by-layer training, MSE loss, Adam (p. 9)
data_channel: Simulated with 3GPP SCM urban micro; AoDs random on angle grid, Rayleigh path powers; 20000 training, 5000 validation, 1000 test samples (pp. 8-9)
test_conditions: Test set from the same generator; SNR, pilot length T, paths s and shared paths sc are swept (Figs. 8-11); training conditions per sweep not stated (pp. 9-12)
baselines: Non-learned: Modified-SP, Enhanced MMV, Oracle LS; learned deep unrolling: LISTA-CPSS, LISTA-GS, and the authors' earlier C-F-BSS (pp. 9-12)
metrics: NMSE and achievable spectral efficiency (ASE) versus SNR, pilot length, number of paths and shared support; training time; running time per sample; multiplications (pp. 9-12)
complexity: Multiplications per iteration (Table V): 8NMT+4NM coarse net, 4NTSa+2NSa+2Sa fine net; running time per sample 0.0079 (Table III); training time 4.70 h (Table IV) (pp. 11-12)
q1_support: p. 8: "We apply the 3GPP Spatial Channel Model (SCM) [37] in" our simulation, urban micro scenario; reference [37] is the MATLAB implementation of 3GPP TR 25.996 (p. 15).
q2_support: p. 9: "in the training, validation and test dataset is K = 20000," so test samples come from the same generator; the sweeps over SNR, pilot length, paths s and shared paths sc (Figs. 8-11) do not state that a network trained under one setting is tested under another.
q3_support: p. 10: "has the closest performance to the stateof-the-art Oracle LS method" and outperforms M-SP and Enhanced MMV (non-learned) and LISTA-CPSS and LISTA-GS (learned unrolled networks [30], [31]) in NMSE, Fig. 8 and Table II; p. 12: "other baseline deep learning schemes are trained with all" layers, Table IV.
q4_support: p. 12: "the computational complexity and the average running time" are compared for all schemes (Tables III and V); p. 13: "Therefore the number of multiplications in each iteration is" O(8NMT + 4NM) for the coarse net.
q5_support: p. 9: "The data in our paper is generated as follows: Firstly," with its own procedure on top of the SCM; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public channel dataset or measurements.
notes: q1 is met on the 3GPP Spatial Channel Model (TR 25.996, p. 8 and ref. [37] on p. 15), a standardized model that is not in the TR 38.901 family listed in the criteria, so the reviewer should confirm it; the authors draw AoDs at random and path powers from a Rayleigh distribution (p. 9), so the SCM is only partly used. Area 2: the learned deep-unrolled network performs downlink channel estimation. No RIS.
